data.name: Marrissa
data.gender_notes: Marrissa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Mariamne,' meaning 'rebellious,' 'bitter,' or 'marine.' This name was borne by a heroine in the New Testament who was the wife of Judas Iscariot and was ultimately beheaded for her faith. The name Marrissa carries the meaning “Bittersweet, rebellious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Marrissa usually hope their child will grow to embody bittersweet, rebellious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Marrissa carries historical roots in the Greek language and biblical connections in the New Testament. While the meaning of 'rebellious' or 'bitter' may not have the most pleasant associations, the name's connection to the determined and faithful Mariamne, wife of Judas, infuses it with a sense of strength, resolve, and intrigue. It implies a fierce independence in its bearer, and the ability to withstand adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: Marrissa, named for a biblical heroine, bears the weight of a spiritual legacy. She is a reminder of the unwavering faith that even those in the midst of turmoil and hardship can possess. Her name invites those who bear it to embody this faith in their own lives, to lean on their strength and resilience in the face of adversity, and to trust that their faith will guide them through even the most challenging of times. It is a name that speaks to the enduring power of faith and the indomitable spirit of those who hold it close.
